title: Assembly Workstation
description: Step-by-step digital work instructions with tool interlocks reduce errors and cycle time on the assembly line
executive_summary: This use case implements a guided assembly workstation that provides operators with step-by-step digital work instructions, integrated tool verification (e.g., smart torque wrenches), barcode/RFID checks for parts, and pick-to-light guidance. The system enforces process order, validates each critical step (poka-yoke), and logs traceability to MES.

business_challenge.industry_context: Drone assembly involves numerous precise steps, torque specs, variant BOMs, and quality checkpoints. Paper instructions and manual sign-offs lead to variability, longer training time, and higher rework risk—especially during product updates and shift handovers.
specific_problems: Inconsistent assembly quality due to manual instructions and human error
Long operator training/onboarding time for complex builds
Limited traceability of who did what step, with which part/tool, and when

business_impact.financial_loss: SAR 650,000 annually from rework, scrap, delayed orders, and extended changeover/training time

selection_criteria: Step-by-step digital work instructions with version control and e-signoff
Tool interlocks/verification (smart torque, barcode/RFID checks, pick-to-light)
Seamless MES/ERP integration for traceability and production reporting

technology_components.details: Industrial PC with barcode/RFID readers and pick-to-light modules
Rule engine with MES integration and electronic traveler
Media-rich instructions with images/video/3D and e-signoff

implementation_details.methodology: Agile rollout across a pilot cell followed by phased expansion

objectives: Integrate tools and validation in one assembly cell

technical_architecture.system_overview: A DWI (Digital Work Instruction) platform running on industrial workstations with connected tools and sensors. The edge rule engine enforces step order and collects traceability, while MES integration logs production history and e-signoffs.

architecture_components.components: Barcode/RFID readers, pick-to-light, smart torque tools, I/O modules
DWI engine, edge rule engine, MES/ERP connector
architecture_components.specifications: Step gating, electronic traveler, API/webhook integrations

architecture_components.components: Operator UI (touchscreen), supervisor dashboards, e-sign portal

security_measures: encrypted data in transit and at rest

future_roadmap.description: Add optional AR guidance for complex sub-assemblies and torque locations
future_roadmap.expected_benefit: Additional 10% error reduction on high-risk steps

future_roadmap.description: Analyze station history to recommend step reordering and media improvements

lessons_learned.description: Photo/diagram-heavy steps outperformed text-only instructions in speed and accuracy
lessons_learned.recommendation: Prioritize visual content and short captions

title: Demanufacturing Workstation
description: Guided teardown and diagnostics recover usable parts, reduce waste, and speed repairs
benefits: 35-pt increase in parts recovery yield to 80%
executive_summary: This use case introduces a demanufacturing workstation that supports structured drone disassembly, fault isolation, and parts grading. Operators follow step-by-step digital instructions on an ESD-safe bench while vision checks, barcode/RFID capture, and functional test fixtures identify failed components. Usable parts are graded (A/B/C), labeled, and returned to stock.

business_challenge.industry_context: Repair, returns, and non-conforming builds create a steady flow of units needing teardown and triage. Without standardized disassembly and diagnostics, shops over-scrap assemblies, buy unnecessary spares, and extend turnaround time.
specific_problems: Unstructured teardown causing damaged recoverable parts
Limited traceability of what failed, why, and which lots were affected
High spare-parts procurement spend due to low reuse rate
Long mean time to diagnose (MTTD) and repair due to manual checks

business_impact.financial_loss: SAR 900,000 annually from excess scrap, avoidable spare-parts purchases, and extended repair cycles

selection_criteria: Step-by-step digital teardown instructions with poka-yoke and e-signoff
Integrated electrical/functional test fixtures for key modules
Parts identification via barcode/RFID + vision to prevent mix-ups
Automatic grading (A/B/C), labeling, and return-to-stock workflow

technology_components.details: Grounded mats, wrist straps, and ionizers
Power, communication, sensor, motor/ESC testing with automated pass/fail

implementation_details.methodology: Iterative deployment: define teardown flows, stand up fixtures, validate tests, then roll out line-wide

objectives: develop/validate test scripts and grading rules

qualitative_impacts: Better supplier feedback via defect evidence

technical_architecture.system_overview: An ESD-compliant workstation ecosystem combining guided instructions, automated tests, vision/ID capture, and grading workflows. The edge rule engine enforces steps and compiles a digital teardown record synced to MES/ERP.

architecture_components.components: Vision camera, barcode/RFID, smart torque, electrical testers, scales
architecture_components.specifications: Millisecond timestamps with test data streamed over MQTT/OPC-UA

architecture_components.components: Teardown DWI, rules engine, test sequencer, MES/ERP connector
architecture_components.specifications: Step gating, automatic pass/fail, grading & labeling, RMA linkage

architecture_components.components: Operator UI, QA dashboard, salvage/return-to-stock reports
architecture_components.specifications: Photo evidence storage, serial/lot traceability, analytics

future_roadmap.description: Train ML models on teardown images + test traces to auto-suggest root causes
future_roadmap.expected_benefit: 20% additional reduction in MTTD and faster triage

future_roadmap.description: Push failure modes to maintenance for design/process feedback and preventive actions
future_roadmap.expected_benefit: Fewer repeats of systemic failures; higher first-time repair rate

lessons_learned.description: Formal A/B/C criteria tied to objective tests removed debate and sped return-to-stock
lessons_learned.recommendation: Publish visual rubrics and auto-link grading to test thresholds

title: Robotic Inspection Station for Drone Arm Dimensional Accuracy
description: An automated quality cell where a robotic arm picks parts from a conveyor, verifies dimensional accuracy with laser scanners, and dispatches approved parts to assembly via Autonomous Mobile Robots (AMRs).
benefits: 97.5% reduction in defective parts reaching assembly
executive_summary: The KACST Industry 4.0 Capability Center implemented a fully automated quality inspection station that serves as the critical link between manufacturing and assembly. The system's robotic arm picks a 3D-printed drone arm from an incoming conveyor belt and places it into a high-precision fixture. Laser sensors scan the component's geometry, which is compared against the source CAD file.

business_challenge.industry_context: For high-performance drones, the precise geometry of components is critical. Even minor warping from the 3D printing process can lead to assembly failures or stress fractures. A robust, automated, and integrated quality check is essential.
specific_problems: Manual transfer of parts between manufacturing and QC created delays, bottlenecks, and risk of damage
Manual dimensional checks using calipers were too slow and inconsistent
No automated way to sort passed and failed parts, leading to potential mix-ups
Inability to provide customers with quantitative quality assurance reports

business_impact.financial_loss: SAR 350,000 annually in scrapped materials, wasted assembly labor, and warranty claims

selection_criteria: The system must measure dimensional accuracy with a tolerance of ±0.05mm
The entire inspection cycle must be under 30 seconds
Must integrate seamlessly with upstream conveyor and downstream AMR fleet
Must use non-contact measurement to avoid cosmetic damage

technology_components.details: Handles all part picking and placing tasks
High-resolution surface geometry and concavity data capture
Optical sensors to signal part arrival
Node-RED based robot calling and confirmation

implementation_details.methodology: Phased systems engineering approach with modular development and testing, using Node-RED as central messaging bus

quantitative_metrics.metric: Assembly Failure Rate (due to part fit)

qualitative_impacts: Guaranteed 100% geometric compliance for every drone arm
Enabled creation of detailed Quality Certificates for each batch
Vastly improved ability to trace defects back to specific 3D printers

technical_architecture.system_overview: The system forms a bridge in the production line. A drone arm arrives on conveyor, triggering a sensor. A 6-axis robot picks the part and places it in a scanning fixture. The 3D laser scanner captures geometry. Node-RED workflow determines Pass/Fail and commands robot to place part in reject bin or AMR.

architecture_components.components: 6-axis Robot, Custom Gripper, Fixture, Conveyor, Dual Safety Scanners
architecture_components.specifications: 270-degree safety monitoring with immediate stop capability
Orchestrates operations and communicates with line systems
REST API dispatch commands to fleet manager

scalability_design: Modular design with exportable Node-RED flows for rapid replication

future_roadmap.description: Analyze dimensional deviation trends and auto-adjust printing parameters
future_roadmap.expected_benefit: Move from defect detection to prevention with self-correcting process

future_roadmap.description: Incorporate AI model to detect cosmetic surface defects in addition to dimensions
future_roadmap.expected_benefit: Single station for 100% geometric and cosmetic inspection

lessons_learned.lesson: Integrate Safety Systems Early in the Design Phase
lessons_learned.description: Initially planned physical fencing, but operator feedback highlighted need for easier access
lessons_learned.recommendation: Treat safety systems as core component from day one, not as add-on

lessons_learned.lesson: Fixture Design is as Critical as Robot Programming
lessons_learned.description: Initial fixture didn't hold part rigidly enough, causing inconsistent scan results
lessons_learned.recommendation: Invest heavily in part-holding fixture design for measurement repeatability

lessons_learned.lesson: Define Go/No-Go Tolerances with Manufacturing and Design Engineers
lessons_learned.description: Software could measure to micron level, but acceptable deviation wasn't initially defined
lessons_learned.recommendation: Establish cross-functional team to define quality standards before coding
